summary:
In the extreme and demanding environments of space exploration, continuous physiological and safety monitoring is critical for astronaut survival. Team "Rockets of Robots Castle" presents Vitalis X, a comprehensive, real-time health and emergency response wearable system integrated with a streamlined web interface.

​What we developed: A robust hardware-software prototype featuring continuous biometric tracking (heart rate and temperature), an automated Fall Detection mechanism, and physical SOS emergency buttons for instant distress signaling.
How it addresses the challenge: By combining real-time vital sign acquisition with instant hazard and emergency alerts, Vitalis X bridges the gap between biomedical sensing and astronaut safety, empowering mission operators with critical decision-making data.

Why it matters: Safety is the cornerstone of any space mission. Our scalable approach ensures that astronauts in hazardous or remote environments are continuously monitored, providing both proactive health tracking and reactive emergency response capabilities.
details:
What it does & How it works: Vitalis X is an advanced, real-time health and safety monitoring system designed for extreme environments. It continuously tracks critical astronauts' physiological parameters—specifically Heart Rate and Temperature—while integrating an automated Fall Detection mechanism and physical SOS emergency buttons for instant distress signaling.

Hardware & Software Tools Used:

Hardware: Microcontrollers, biometric sensors, temperature sensors, push buttons for SOS, and accelerometer/gyroscope modules for fall detection.

Software & Interfaces: HTML/CSS for the web dashboard interface, and local prototyping tools for simulation and data acquisition.

Key Features & Innovation:

1. Proactive Health Tracking: Real-time data streaming of vital signs to ensure early anomaly detection.

2. Reactive Emergency Response: Immediate physical SOS alerts and automated fall detection to protect personnel in hazardous situations.

3. User-Friendly Interface: Clean web dashboard providing mission operators with clear, actionable telemetry data.

Intended Impact: Safeguarding human lives in high-risk environments by bridging biomedical sensing with instant emergency response workflows, ensuring mission safety and operational readiness.
